children.text: Bud Light uses ethos by placing well known public figures Shane Gillis, Post Malone, and Peyton Manning together in the commercial. Each celebrity brings a recognizable persona and connects with a different audience. Peyton Manning appeals to football and NFL fans, Post Malone appeals to music and pop-culture audiences, and Shane Gillis connects with comedy fans and his online following. Their familiarity gives Bud Light credibility. It also is helping the brand reach several overlapping groups at once. Bud Light does not choose to rely on a traditional spokesperson, they use personalities that viewers already recognize and trust.

Pathos is used through humor in the commercial when the keg begins rolling down the hill and everyone reacts as if something has gone terribly wrong. The situation is exaggerated because nobody is actually in danger. However, the characters treat saving the Bud Light like an emergency. This creates a playful tone. The keg of Bud Light is seen as an important ingredient for the wedding to continue. Bud Light is not just trying to tell the viewer how great their beer is, but rather trying to connect their product to feelings of fun and excitement.

The wedding guests dramatically chasing the keg creates humor through exaggeration. Pathos is also used to create humor by showing the guests falling down the hill. The guests willingness to tumble down a hill over a keg makes Bud Light seem like a key part to the celebration. This use of pathos is meant to make the audience laugh while also connecting the product with the excitement of the party. The excessive tone makes the advertisement more ike entertainment rather than just a beer commercial.

While the wedding guests chase the keg down the hill, Whitney Houston's “I Will Always Love You” begins playing while people are falling and crashing into each other. The emotional song does not match the goofy situation. This creates a large part of the humor. The visual modality of guests chasing the keg down the hill combined with the audio modality of the song creates a light hearted humorous tone. The affordances are seen in the visual and audio modalities in this clip as well as the ad uses popular music and creative scenes.

Gillis alienates himself from the rest of the wedding by refusing to run down the hill after the keg. While everyone else crashes into each other, he states that the situation is “not necessary” and eventually points out that there is a trail. This moment fits the sarcastic style that his audience already associates him with. Budlight does not make Gillis completely change his personality to promote their beer. The commercial allows him to act like his usual self. This is important rhetorically because the advertisement feels like Gillis is stopping his normal content to give a sales pitch. Bud Light is using his established persona to make the advertising feel like part of the entertainment.

When everyone reaches the bottom of the hill, the keg is recovered and Bud Light can finally be served to the guests. The chaos seems to become worth it because the characters are able to continue drinking together. Peyton Manning makes a comment about it being a “heck of a wedding” which treats the entire disaster as part of the fun. The emotions of friendship and celebration are targeted. This supports the larger message of the commercial that Bud Light is connected and essential for memorable social experiences. The advertisement is not directly selling the taste or quality of the beer. It is selling the idea that Bud Light belongs at parties, sporting events, weddings, and other situations where people are coming together.

At the end of the advertisement Gillis tells the bride that it was a great ceremony before turning toward the camera and saying, “I give it a week.” This final joke is very important because it fits with Shanes comedic persona and gives Gillis the last word with his usual sarcastic style.This use of humor creates pathos by trying to make the audience laugh. This entertainment is also part of the commercial’s persuasion. The purpose of this is to make viewers enjoy and remember the advertisement. Bud Light is enticing them to remember the brand with humor, fun, and being social. Bud Light, the commercial persuades them to view the brand positively and hopes the viewer chooses it when they are in similar social settings.

Gillis posted the commercial directly to his personal Instagram. The advertisement reaches viewers through a different modern medium. Although it appears like traditional television commercial the medium is important to note. Instagram allows the video to circulate through Gillis’s own follower base. This means people are likely to encounter the advertisement because they already follow him. The platform also gives viewers the affordances to like, comment, and share the post. This can help the advertisement spread beyond its original audience due to interaction boosting the algorithm. These affordances make Gillis more than just an actor in the commercial due to his own social media account becomes part of how Bud Light distributes and promotes the advertisement. It makes me view him as more of a public ambassador of the brand rather than just a temporary sponsor.
